# Results — Study 371 (CBOE SKEW Index)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The CBOE **SKEW** index — the
"black-swan" gauge that reads the price of out-of-the-money S&P 500 puts relative to
at-the-money options — tested as a **crash warning the VIX can't give**. We ask the only
question that matters: does SKEW carry forward-return or tail-event information **beyond** what
VIX already prices? Real tape: yfinance daily closes for `^SKEW`, `^VIX` and `SPY`. Offline &
deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily closes — `^SKEW`, `^VIX`, `SPY` (public, no key) |
| Window | 1993-01-29 → 2026-06-18 (**8,330** joint trading days; **33.4** years) |
| SKEW level | mean **123.7** (CBOE SKEW; 100 = symmetric, higher = pricier OTM put tail) |
| VIX level | mean **19.5**; **corr(SKEW, VIX) = −0.19** (the two move *apart*, not together) |
| Entry / costs | 1-day execution lag; 2-bps one-way cost × turnover on the costed sleeve |

> **Why this is the honest test.** SKEW and VIX are both option-implied; the believers' claim is
> that SKEW is *additive* — it warns when VIX is calm. So the decisive object is the **SKEW
> coefficient in a forward-return regression that already controls for VIX**, read with
> **HAC (Newey-West)** standard errors (overlapping windows are heavily autocorrelated). A raw
> bucket *t* that pretends 800+ overlapping days are independent is a trap — there are only
> ~a dozen *distinct* high-SKEW episodes in the whole tape.

## The decisive test — forward SPY return on SKEW **controlling for VIX** (HAC *t*)

Predictors standardised (per-1σ); forward return entered 1 day after the signal; Newey-West
lags = horizon. `t_skew` is SKEW's *incremental* coefficient once VIX is in the regression.

| horizon | n | β(SKEW)/1σ | **t(SKEW)** | β(VIX)/1σ | t(VIX) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-month | 8,308 | +0.06% | **+0.35** | +0.43% | +1.54 |
| 3-month | 8,266 | +0.25% | **+0.49** | +0.89% | +1.13 |

SKEW's incremental *t* is **+0.35 / +0.49** — nowhere near the **t ≥ 2** bar, and the sign is
*positive* (higher SKEW → marginally *higher* forward returns, the opposite of a crash warning).
Even VIX itself isn't significant at these horizons. **SKEW adds nothing beyond VIX.**

## The directional bucket — and why its "significant" *t* is a mirage

High-SKEW days = top decile (SKEW ≥ 141). Forward return after high-SKEW days vs the rest:

| horizon | n high-SKEW days | hi mean | rest mean | hi win | rest win | naive Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-month | 831 | +1.02% | +0.97% | 69% | 65% | +0.37 | 0.619 |
| 3-month | 827 | +2.37% | +2.94% | 71% | 72% | **−2.33** | 0.026 |

The 3-month bucket's **−2.33** *t* looks like a real "high SKEW → weaker returns" effect. It is
**not**. Those 827 high-SKEW days are not 827 independent observations — they cluster into only
**~13 distinct episodes**, and the overlapping 3-month windows are strongly autocorrelated. A
**circular block bootstrap** (block = horizon), which respects that structure, deflates it:

| horizon | observed hi−rest | block-bootstrap SE | **block *t*** | distinct episodes |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-month | +0.05% | 0.38% | **+0.13** | ~23 |
| 3-month | −0.57% | 1.13% | **−0.50** | ~13 |

The honest, autocorrelation-respecting *t* is **+0.13 / −0.50** — flat. The naive −2.33 was a
**pseudo-replication artifact**: counting overlapping days as independent. There is no
directional edge.

## The tail-warning claim — high SKEW precedes *fewer* crashes, not more

SKEW's whole reputation is *tail* insurance. So: after a high-SKEW day, is a forward **tail
event** (a drawdown over the next month) more likely than usual?

| tail definition (1-month forward) | high-SKEW rate | base rate | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| drawdown worse than −10% | **1.7%** | 4.4% | 1.000 |
| drawdown worse than −5% | **13.7%** | 17.3% | 0.998 |

The crash rate after a high SKEW is **lower** than the unconditional base rate. The "warning"
fires *less* often before trouble than a random day does. The placebo *p* ≈ 1.0 confirms it: a
random draw essentially always shows more tail risk than the high-SKEW set. **The black-swan
gauge does not light up before black swans** — high SKEW marks *complacency-priced* tails that
mostly do not arrive.

## Tradability — fading high SKEW just costs you return

The believers' trade: de-risk to cash while SKEW is in its top decile, hold SPY otherwise
(1-day lag, 2-bps one-way × turnover; SPY price-only proxy, no dividends).

| | CAGR | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|
| **Fade-high-SKEW sleeve** (10% of days in cash) | **9.04%** | **0.57** |
| Buy-and-hold SPY (same tape) | 10.94% | 0.65 |

Sitting out the highest-SKEW 10% of days **lowers** both return and Sharpe — because those days
are *not* disproportionately followed by losses. There is no deployable edge; the sleeve is a
strict drag.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful, and the knob works

A deterministic (SKEW, VIX, SPY) panel with corr(SKEW, VIX) ≈ 0.70 and a **planted-edge knob**
that makes the VIX-*orthogonal* part of SKEW depress next-day drift. The VIX-controlled HAC
regression must recover it — and must stay quiet when the knob is off:

| planted edge | n | β(SKEW)/1σ | **t(SKEW)** |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.0** (no edge) | 7,978 | +0.11% | **+0.42** |
| **+0.0005** (real edge planted) | 7,978 | −0.76% | **−2.85** |

With **no** planted edge the test stays at **t = +0.42** (it cannot manufacture significance);
with a genuine VIX-orthogonal edge it lights up at **t = −2.85** with the correct negative sign.
The machinery is unbiased — so the real-tape **t = +0.35** is what an *absent* incremental
SKEW signal looks like, not a power failure.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** SKEW's forward-return coefficient **controlling for VIX** is **t = +0.35
  (1m) / +0.49 (3m)** — far below t ≥ 2, and *positive*-signed. The lone "significant" bucket
  *t* (−2.33 at 3m) is a pure overlapping-window / pseudo-replication artifact: only ~13
  distinct episodes, block-bootstrap *t* = −0.50. SKEW carries **no information beyond VIX**.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Fading high SKEW **underperforms** buy-and-hold (9.04% vs 10.94%
  CAGR; Sharpe 0.57 vs 0.65). No edge to harvest; acting on the "warning" is a drag.
- **Warns before crashes? — BUSTED.** After a high SKEW the forward tail-event rate is **lower**
  than the base rate (1.7% vs 4.4% for −10% drawdowns; placebo p ≈ 1.0). The black-swan gauge
  fires *before calm*, not before crashes — it prices the tails the market *fears*, which are
  precisely the ones that mostly don't happen.
